programs.name: CEHG Fellowships (Center for Computational, Evolutionary and Human Genomics)
programs.requirements: Application with a research statement (2 pages max), and a nominating letter from the Stanford faculty sponsor for postdoc applicants. Full details are in the Application Instructions PDF, which I did not open.
programs.eligibility: Graduate students entering the final year of their PhD and early postdoctoral fellows. A search snippet said international candidates may apply. The page itself does not confirm this.
programs.deadline_text: The 2026-27 cycle is closed. The next window is not announced.

programs.name: Stanford Genetics and Genomics Certificate (Stanford Center for Professional Development, online)
programs.requirements: Two required and four elective courses, per the listing. Fees and prerequisites not verified.
programs.eligibility: Open to professionals and external learners. I did not confirm this on the official page.
programs.deadline_text: Ongoing enrolment per search snippet. Not verified on the page.

programs.name: Stanford Genetics AI Longevity Lab Certificate course
programs.requirements: Course fee of about $500 per course, per the listing. No prerequisites were stated.
programs.eligibility: Open to everyone, in person or by Zoom, per the listing.
programs.deadline_text: No dates found.

programs.name: HMS Division of Medical Sciences (DMS) Visiting Fellows Program
programs.requirements: Faculty Advisor at HMS who agrees to host the research; a Secondary Faculty Advisor (typically same department); online application plus Assurance of Academic and Financial Support; funding at HMS graduate-student level from the host advisor, the home institution or an individual fellowship; reduced tuition and health fees each semester
programs.eligibility: Students enrolled in research doctoral programs at universities outside the U.S. who plan to do lab research at Harvard Medical School; non-degree GSAS status; must enter the US in F-1 status and be enrolled full-time
programs.location: Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA
programs.duration: Organized by semester (Fall start Sept 1, Spring start Feb 1); total length not stated
programs.deadline_text: March 1 for Fall entry, October 1 for Spring entry (strictly enforced). The October 1, 2026 Spring 2027 deadline has pas

programs.name: Harvard Chan Bioinformatics Core: Advanced Topics in NGS Data Analysis workshops (scRNA-seq, pseudobulk, spatial transcriptomics, differential expression)
programs.requirements: Registration via the training schedule page (opens about 3 weeks before each workshop); fees vary by affiliation and are listed on the separate workshop pricing page
programs.eligibility: Open to external participants (external academic rate exists); online via Zoom, so no visa needed
programs.location: Online (Zoom), Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
programs.duration: 4 half-day sessions per workshop (e.g. Introduction to scRNA-seq Feb 16, 19, 23, 26, 2027; Spatial Transcriptomics Jan 26, 29, Feb 2, 5, 2027)
programs.deadline_text: Registration opens ~3 weeks before each workshop; some are already open, others TBD

programs.name: Harvard Chan Bioinformatics Core: Cells to Insights boot camp (Intro to R and scRNA-seq)
programs.requirements: Registration via the training schedule page; boot camp registration opens ~3 months before
programs.eligibility: Open to external participants (pricing tiers on workshop pricing page); online
programs.duration: One week: Dec 7-11, 2026 (registration open) and Jun 7-11, 2027 (registration TBD)
programs.deadline_text: Registration for the June 2027 camp opens about 3 months before

programs.name: Harvard Chan Bioinformatics Core: Current Topics in Bioinformatics (free monthly modules, e.g. Multiomics I-III)
programs.requirements: Register online; no fee
programs.eligibility: Open to the greater Harvard community; external participation is not confirmed on the page I read
programs.duration: Monthly half-day, 9:30am-12:30pm (Dec 16, 2026; Jan 20, Feb 17, Mar 17, Apr 14, May 26, Jun 16, 2027)
programs.deadline_text: Registration opens about 3 weeks before each module

programs.name: Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center Postdoctoral Fellowship (Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard)
programs.requirements: Experience in machine learning, statistics or applied mathematics relevant to biomedical research (biology experience helpful but optional). Fellow chooses a computational mentor and a biomedical mentor from Broad/MIT/Harvard faculty. Apply via AJO portal (broad.io/ewsc-postdoc).
programs.eligibility: Postdoctoral researchers, so applicable after PhD completion. International eligibility and visa terms are not stated on the page; contact ericandwendyschmidtcenter@broadinstitute.org.
programs.duration: 1 year initially, renewable up to 3 years
programs.deadline_text: Applications for 2027 open; rolling review begins after 2026-12-22; start on or after 2027-07-01 (flexible)

programs.name: Schmidt Fellows Program (Broad Institute)
programs.requirements: Early-career scientists from mathematical, computational or physical sciences; independent fellows with PI status (not postdocs).
programs.eligibility: International eligibility not stated; questions to schmidtfellows@broadinstitute.org. Page says the program is not currently recruiting.
programs.duration: 3 years initially, possible extension of 1-2 years
programs.deadline_text: Not currently recruiting; no deadline listed

programs.name: Visiting Student Research Collaborator (VSRC), Princeton Graduate School
programs.requirements: A Princeton faculty sponsor, for example in Lewis-Sigler, QCB, Computer Science or Molecular Biology. Full-time, on-site research. No credit courses or transcript. No remote work, TA post or other paid job. Fees and cost-of-living rates are listed on the page for 2026-27. I did not verify the other application documents.
programs.eligibility: Advanced degree candidates enrolled in a graduate program at another institution. I did not verify the rules for international students or the visa process.
programs.duration: Not verified. The search summary mentions a Summer 2027 application cycle.
programs.deadline_text: The summary says the Summer 2027 application opens in December 2026. I found no deadline date.

programs.name: Lewis-Sigler Institute opportunities and postdoctoral listings (including Lewis-Sigler Fellows and Scholars)
programs.requirements: Postdocs are normally applied for through Princeton's online academic positions site. The Institute's own page says it is not accepting Lewis-Sigler Scholars applications at this time. The Lewis-Sigler Fellows are independent early-career fellows funded for five years.
programs.eligibility: These are postdoctoral roles for people who have finished their PhD. This is not open to the student now. It is relevant only as a later step. I did not verify the international eligibility.
programs.duration: Fellows are funded for 5 years. Scholars are 0-2 years from the PhD.
programs.deadline_text: No current call found. One third-party posting for an Integrative Genomics postdoc lists a 2027-02-27 deadline, but I di

programs.name: Princeton Presidential Postdoctoral Research Fellows Program
programs.requirements: Nomination by a Princeton faculty sponsor. This comes from a third-party listing only.
programs.eligibility: Postdoctoral candidates after the PhD. This is not open to the student now. I did not verify the international eligibility.
programs.duration: One year, renewable for a second year. This is from a third-party listing.
programs.deadline_text: Princeton's news page dated 2026-10-29 announces the 2026 cohort. A third-party listing gives 2026-11-13 for nominations

programs.name: Visiting Student Researcher (VSR) appointment, Caltech Graduate Studies Office (host lab in Biology & Biological Engineering, Computing + Mathematical Sciences, or another division)
programs.requirements: A Caltech faculty member must sponsor you and submit the Visiting Student Request form with proof of faculty support. You contact a lab yourself to find a host; the application goes through the host, not through you.
programs.eligibility: Open to people who hold a bachelor's degree and are current graduate students at another institution, so a UBC PhD student qualifies. Visits last 1 month to 1 year and can't be renewed. VSRs get no course credit and no Caltech payroll stipend. The Graduate Special Student category is the route if you need a stipend or transcript credit. Most international VSRs need F-1 status (I-20) from Caltech's international office.
programs.deadline_text: No fixed deadline; the host faculty member submits the request. I did not check how far ahead the request must be filed.

programs.name: DataSAI for Neuroscience Summer School (Chen Center for Data Science and AI)
programs.requirements: Not verified. The 2026 and 2027 application details were not found. The application page I tried returned a 404.
programs.eligibility: The search summary said past sessions were for Caltech neuroscience trainees (graduate students, postdocs, staff). I couldn't confirm whether outside students can apply. The topic is neuroscience data analysis, so it is only loosely relevant to cancer genomics.
programs.location: Caltech or the Seeley Mudd estate, San Marino, California, USA (2023 and 2025 sessions)
programs.deadline_text: No current call found

programs.name: CRUK Cambridge Institute – Visiting Students
programs.requirements: Identify a matching research group; email CV, a letter from your home university confirming the placement counts as valid study, and a covering letter with intended dates and project/scope. English-language requirement applies if not from a majority English-speaking country.
programs.eligibility: Students registered at another institution who meet University of Cambridge criteria; international applicants accepted. Must self-fund, including visa costs. The Institute hosts about 30 visiting students a year.
programs.deadline_text: No deadline listed; contact mailbox-acdev@cruk.cam.ac.uk for timing

programs.name: EMBL-EBI–Sanger Postdoctoral (ESPOD) Fellowship
programs.requirements: Cover letter, CV, two recent reference letters. Choose up to 3 of 8 predefined projects, or propose a self-designed project (up to 1,000 words) that involves at least one EMBL-EBI group and one Sanger group and is approved by the group leaders beforehand.
programs.eligibility: Postdoctoral-level scheme, so relevant to the student only after the PhD. The page lists no eligibility criteria. Contact espod@ebi.ac.uk.
programs.location: Wellcome Genome Campus, Hinxton, Cambridge, UK
programs.deadline_text: 2026 call closed; interviews 10 Dec 2026. The next call is not yet announced.

programs.name: Wellcome Connecting Science – Courses and Conferences (Hinxton), e.g. Scalable Genomics and Pangenomics, Cancer Genomic Epidemiology
programs.requirements: Application via the course page. Fees are subsidised by Connecting Science, and bursaries are offered for some courses and conferences. The 2027 schedule was not found.
programs.eligibility: Open postgraduate courses with international participants. Check each course page for eligibility and bursary terms; contact courses@wellcomeconnectingscience.org.
programs.location: Wellcome Genome Campus, Hinxton, Cambridge, UK (some courses held in partner countries)
programs.duration: Varies; the 2026 pangenomics course ran 11–16 Oct 2026
programs.deadline_text: Varies by event; the 2027 listings were not found

programs.name: Wellcome Genome Campus – Upcoming events and training
programs.requirements: Varies by event; see the listing.
programs.eligibility: Varies by event. Financial support is available for some events via Wellcome Connecting Science.
programs.deadline_text: See the individual event pages

programs.name: Independent Visiting Research Student (UCL central scheme; applied to a bioinformatics, genomics or computational biology group, e.g. UCL Genetics Institute, Cancer Institute or Centre for Computation
programs.requirements: Evidence of current PhD registration. Confirmation from the home institution that you are a registered research degree student. A UCL academic in your field who agrees to supervise the visit, often in writing. Some departments also ask for a CV or research proposal. Apply through UCL's online portal and select Visiting Research.
programs.eligibility: PhD students from other universities, including international students. The research must support your home PhD project. Pro-rata tuition is payable. Check visa requirements yourself, because some departments do not help with visas.
programs.duration: 3 to 12 months. Visits of about a term or less use a separate informal route through the department.
programs.deadline_text: Not confirmed. Apply once a UCL supervisor has agreed.

programs.name: Genetic Epidemiology Short Course (UCL Division of Psychiatry)
programs.requirements: Not verified. The course covers genome-wide association studies and polygenic scores.
programs.eligibility: Not verified. Whether external and international participants can attend, and any fee, are unconfirmed.
programs.deadline_text: Not found

programs.name: Oxford Statistical Genomics Summer School (Dept. for Continuing Education, with WHG, BDI and Statistics)
programs.requirements: Not verified for the current year. The 2022 announcement gives no application requirements.
programs.eligibility: Aimed at researchers from academia and industry. Financial assistance is available to under-represented groups through a separate application. International eligibility not stated.
programs.deadline_text: No 2027 date or deadline found. The only page I saw is the 2022 announcement.

programs.name: Oxford Machine Learning School (OxML), health and biology module
programs.requirements: Not verified. This comes from a December 2025 announcement of the 2026 edition.
programs.eligibility: Not verified. The announcement lists computational biology topics such as proteomics, genomics and multi-omics.
programs.deadline_text: No 2027 edition found. Check the OxML website.

programs.name: Real World Evidence Summer School (OMOP), Oxford Population Health, with Trueta bursaries
programs.requirements: Not verified. This course is about real-world health data, so it is only loosely related to cancer genomics.
programs.eligibility: The 2025 edition offered Trueta bursaries covering attendance and college accommodation. Eligibility for external or international PhD students is not verified.
programs.deadline_text: A 2026 edition existed. No 2027 dates found.

programs.name: Arc Science Fellows (early-career PI / postdoc-level fellowship)
programs.requirements: Early-career scientists planning high-risk, original research; the page says the doctorate should be completed within about two years of program entry (the page's structured data and main text differ slightly)
programs.eligibility: Open to applicants from any institution. The page doesn't state citizenship or visa rules, and it is not open to a first-year PhD student now. It is a possible future route after graduation.
programs.location: Arc Institute, Palo Alto, CA, USA
programs.deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page

programs.name: Arc AIxBio Fellows Program for Undergrads
programs.requirements: Teams of 2-3 undergraduates, based in North America, with strong technical skills and a commitment to open, reproducible research; 6-12 months, about 10 hours per week
programs.eligibility: Undergraduates only. No citizenship restrictions. The page's FAQ on graduate students is not answered in the text I retrieved. A PhD student is almost certainly ineligible.
programs.location: Virtual, with Arc researchers as mentors
programs.deadline_text: 2027 applications expected to open in January 2027

programs.name: Arc Virtual Cell Challenge 2026
programs.requirements: Build ML models predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell contexts (zero-shot). The grand prize is $100,000.
programs.eligibility: Open competition. I did not verify the details on the registration site.
programs.deadline_text: Not verified. A 'Winners and Wrap-Up (November 2026)' article is listed, so the challenge may already be finished.

programs.name: Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center Postdoctoral Fellowship (2027 cohort)
programs.requirements: Research interests in machine learning, statistics or applied mathematics that could advance biomedical research. ML or related experience is critical. Biology or medicine background is optional. Fellows choose a computational and a biomedical mentor from Broad, MIT or Harvard faculty. Apply through the AJO portal (broad.io/ewsc-postdoc).
programs.eligibility: Postdoctoral applicants, so relevant to the student only after the PhD. The page does not state international eligibility or visa details. Contact ericandwendyschmidtcenter@broadinstitute.org.
programs.deadline_text: Applications open for 2027. Rolling review begins after 2026-12-22. Start on or after 2027-07-01.

programs.name: BroadE workshops (hands-on technology and computational training)
programs.requirements: Not stated. The page lists no current schedule, and an earlier search result said none were scheduled.
programs.eligibility: Open to Broad staff and to researchers at MIT, Harvard and Harvard-affiliated hospitals. External attendees are not mentioned, so a UBC student is likely ineligible.
programs.deadline_text: No dates published

programs.name: Broad Summer Research Program (BSRP)
programs.requirements: Online form, transcripts, CV, essays and two recommendation letters. Full-time for 9 weeks.
programs.eligibility: Undergraduates only, non-graduating, so a PhD student cannot apply. Included for completeness. The 2027 cycle details are due to be updated from October 2026.
programs.deadline_text: 2026 cycle closed on 2026-01-11. The 2027 deadline has not been announced.

programs.name: Scripps Research Translational Institute (SRTI) Student Research Internship Program
programs.requirements: Interest in genomics or mHealth translational research. The program is aimed at students in health sciences, statistics, and computational or computer science. Separate application from SURF.
programs.eligibility: Students in high school, college, or professional or graduate training. Applicants generally need to be enrolled in a US academic program, typically on F-1 or J-1 status, with work authorization (CPT or AT) approved before the start. A Canadian-enrolled PhD student may not qualify, so confirm with the program before applying.
programs.deadline_text: Applications opened 2026-11-23; deadline March 30, 2027; notices April 30, 2027

programs.name: Scripps Research Fellows Program (independent postdoctoral fellowship)
programs.requirements: Application through Interfolio. Applicants should have recently earned (or be about to earn) a PhD, MD, DVM, or equivalent, or have spent under a year as a biomedical postdoc. Applied research projects are not eligible.
programs.eligibility: Open to external applicants, and international scholars can apply. Scripps helps with US legal status. This is a postdoc scheme, so the student could apply near the end of their PhD, not now.
programs.duration: 3 years of funding plus lab space; anticipated start Fall 2027
programs.deadline_text: First review round covers applications submitted by Dec 31, 2026. Applications are accepted until the position is filled

programs.name: Visiting student / research internship (J-1 Short-term or Research Scholar)
programs.requirements: Applicants must find and get agreement from a Scripps PI host, then provide a CV and details of financial support. The PI contacts the International Services Office to start visa sponsorship. Applicants must stay enrolled at their home institution.
programs.eligibility: International students enrolled in a degree program outside the US who come for thesis or dissertation research. This fits a Canadian PhD student. J-1 Scholar status is for students funded mainly by their home university. A J Intern route with third-party sponsor fees applies to students funded mainly by personal funds. The Scripps ISO does not place students.
programs.duration: Not stated. Confirm with the ISO.
programs.deadline_text: No fixed deadline. Arranged directly with a host PI.

programs.name: SRTI T32 Postdoctoral Training Program (translational)
programs.requirements: A verified PhD. A T32 participating Scripps faculty mentor is required. The proposed research must be judged translational by the T32 and K12 program directors.
programs.eligibility: Applicants must be US citizens or meet an equivalent status under NIH T32 rules, so a Canadian citizen without US permanent residency is likely ineligible. This is a postdoc scheme only.
programs.deadline_text: No deadline or open status listed on the page.

programs.name: NYGC Postdoctoral Training Program (postdoc positions posted by lab)
programs.requirements: PhD or completed PhD requirements. Apply to a posted position or contact a faculty member directly. The process usually includes interviews, a research seminar and references.
programs.eligibility: Anyone who holds or has completed a PhD. International applicants are supported: NYGC's Office of International Services helps with visas, and postdocs are typically sponsored on J-1 status. The page lists reimbursement for some immigration costs and up to $3,000 for international relocation. This is a future option for the student, not something they can apply to as a current first-year PhD student.
programs.duration: Usually a 3-year initial term, which may be extended
programs.deadline_text: No fixed deadline on the page. Positions are posted on a rolling basis, or you can contact faculty directly.

programs.name: NYGC Genomic AI Fellows
programs.requirements: PhD in computer science, computational biology, genomics or a related quantitative field. Deep expertise in deep learning, foundation models and large-scale model training. Interest in or experience with gene regulation, epigenomics or the genetics of complex disease. A track record of leading original research on complex multi-modal data.
programs.eligibility: Aimed at early-career scientists who already hold a PhD. The student cannot apply as a current PhD student. The page does not say whether international applicants are eligible, nor does it give the application status. It links to an application portal (jobs.silkroad.com, posting 779), which I did not open.
programs.location: Not stated on the page; NYGC is in New York, NY
programs.deadline_text: Not stated on the page

programs.name: NYGC Summer Internship Program
programs.requirements: Applicants must be undergraduate students in a related course of study.
programs.eligibility: Undergraduates only, so a PhD student is not eligible. The page says it is closed for 2026 and to check back for opportunities in 2027. It is listed only so the student knows it exists.
programs.deadline_text: The 2026 program is closed. No 2027 dates have been announced.

programs.name: Biohub PhD Summer Internship (Redwood Shores; 2026 cycle seen)
programs.requirements: Current PhD student in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, structural biology or a related field, with substantial wet-lab experience. Fully on-site. No housing or housing stipend. This is a wet-lab role, so it fits computational work only loosely.
programs.eligibility: Open to current PhD students. The search snippet did not say whether students from other countries can apply. A US visa would probably be needed.
programs.duration: 10 weeks (16 Jun to 21 Aug 2026 in the 2026 cycle)
programs.deadline_text: The 2026 cycle made offers on a rolling basis, all expected to be accepted by early March 2026. I did not find a 2027 po

programs.name: Biohub AI Research Scientist Intern (PhD-level, ML/AI, computational biology)
programs.requirements: A third-party listing says active PhD enrolment in ML/AI, computational biology, physics, applied math or a related quantitative field, for a 3-month role paid at $88/hour. The official Biohub careers page lists the role but shows no details, so these requirements are unverified.
programs.eligibility: Unverified. The official page says nothing on visa sponsorship or work authorization.

programs.deadline_text: No current call found. Check the official page.

programs.deadline_text: Final deadline 27 May 2025, 3 p.m. PT. The page states 'This RFA is closed'.

programs.name: Cancer Genomic Epidemiology (Wellcome Connecting Science course at Sanger/Genome Campus)
programs.requirements: Application via the course site; bursaries available (bursary deadline same as application deadline). Further requirements not listed on the courses page.

programs.requirements: Application via course site; laboratory-type course. Further requirements not listed.

programs.eligibility: Researchers in population/comparative genomics, evolution or large-scale sequencing; international applicants welcome, and many nationalities need no UK visa for the course.

programs.requirements: Apply via the EMBL jobs page with a cover letter, CV and two reference letters. Choose up to 3 of 8 predefined projects, or self-propose a project (up to 1,000 words) approved by the group leaders. The 2026 call used EMBL stipend rates.

programs.name: Career Returner Fellowship
programs.requirements: Application form, covering letter and CV. Applicants should contact LMB Group Leaders beforehand
programs.eligibility: Not currently in a scientific research role, with a break from research of at least 12 months. PhD or postdoc experience in a relevant area. Nationality rules not stated
programs.deadline_text: 2026 round closed 17 May 2026; next round not announced
